maya (sec-eng): Heads up — found CVE-2026-1023 in libkms-crypto (transitive via kms-client@2.1.0). Affects private/on-prem images that bundle libkms. Potential HKDF auth bypass when agent socket is accessible.

jon (eng-platform): ouch. Which customers are impacted? Dedicated hosted infra ok?

maya (sec-eng): telemetry shows 3 flagged customers (acme, aurora, data-ops-prod). Dedicated hosted endpoints generally safe unless they use our customer images or proxy with customer-managed keys.

sam (eng-runtime): exploitability? remote RCE or local auth bypass?

maya (sec-eng): auth bypass in HKDF step — requires local access to agent unix socket or misconfigured RBAC. High risk for on-prem with lax socket perms. Recommend P1 for Private, P2 for Dedicated.

lee (sre): can we do a quick mitigation (RBAC tighten + audit rules) before shipping a patch?

maya (sec-eng): yes — mitigations: 1) enforce agent socket perms (chown 640 + proper group), 2) systemd drop-in to restrict access, 3) auditd rule to detect unexpected opens to /var/run/redwood-agent.sock. But ultimately need patched lib.

priya (eng-security): is there a patched release upstream?

maya (sec-eng): upstream published libkms-crypto 2.1.2 with the fix. We need to backport to our base images: r2025.4 and r2026.1. Options: rebuild images with 2.1.2 or ship a runtime wrapper that disables the vulnerable HKDF codepath via env var.

sam (eng-runtime): wrapper is faster but risky; could cause behavioral drift. Rebuilds take longer, esp for air-gapped on-prem customers.

jon (eng-platform): propose two-track: immediate mitigations + wrapper env var for customers who can toggle config (fast), and schedule hotfix image rebuilds for r2025.4 and r2026.1 tagged per-customer. Image tag convention: r2025.4-hotfix-cve1023.{customer}.

maya (sec-eng): agree. Also update RBAC docs and send security advisory. Who drafts the advisory?

priya (eng-security): I can draft advisory and coordinate customer outreach. Need canonical customer list and account owners.

deploy-bot: runbook created: sec/2026-1023-backport — checklist items added (mitigation, hotfix builds, advisory).

lee (sre): branching strategy? we should avoid one-off long-lived customer branches.

sam (eng-runtime): create hotfix branches off release tags: e.g. release/r2025.4 -> hotfix/CVE-1023, release/r2026.1 -> hotfix/CVE-1023. CI produces signed images and per-customer manifests.

jon (eng-platform): +1. Also add automated diff manifest so on-prem customers can apply a delta if they prefer partial patch.

maya (sec-eng): action items: @priya draft advisory by EOD, @sam + @jon coordinate hotfix builds tomorrow AM, @lee add systemd drop-in to ops docs + push audit detection rule, @maya open Jira sec-1023 and assign owners.

priya (eng-security): noted — will cc AE owners and include templated emails.

sec-bot: reminder — incident severity not set. Suggested severity: Sev3.

maya (sec-eng): set to Sev2 for private deployments (higher risk).

sec-bot: incident severity updated to Sev2.

sam (eng-runtime): quick systemd drop-in snippet for docs:

```
[Service]
ProtectSystem=strict
RestrictAddressFamilies=AF_UNIX
ReadWritePaths=/var/run/redwood-agent.sock
```

lee (sre): also add udev/socket perms in init and a note to check unit file for custom installs.

jon (eng-platform): proposed timeline: mitigation env var + systemd guidance within 4 hours, advisory + customer contact list by EOD, hotfix images within 48 hours, fully tested on-prem images within 72 hours. Can we reserve build capacity?

maya (sec-eng): yes if infra reserves a Dedicated build slot. I'll request it now.

priya (eng-security): I'll prepare templates and start contacting account owners once I have the list.

lee (sre): tagging for tracking: sec/cve-1023, infra/hotfix-build, sre/audit-detection.

maya (sec-eng): thanks team. Any objections? :thumbsup:

jon (eng-platform): :thumbsup:

sam (eng-runtime): :thumbsup:

maya (sec-eng): closing thread — will update Jira and runbook when done.
